F — Render into CT: realistic, scanner-matched insertion

Letter folder F_render/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/F_render/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

Cell states → HU from an LIDC-fitted lesion library; supersampled partial volume; additive-delta insertion (vessel max-rule, ground-glass α-blend); 3-D PSF + noise from the host scan's own fingerprint (MTF from the air–skin edge, local NPS and σ), inserted into the full 3-D host volume. 2-D slices only as a final export. Upgrade path: projection-domain insertion on Mayo Siemens raw data via XCIST, then a NAEOTOM Alpha approximation.

How to run (sim commands)

F is classical, so no quantum labels apply. All commands run with cwd = reverse-engineering/ and conda-base python. Extra dependencies are in requirements.txt. Every run writes F_render/runs/<ts>-<tag>/run.json (gitignored).

# render: growth snapshot → hybrid_volume (defaults: shared/stubs/ + the fitted library)
python -m F_render.src.render                         # follow-up snapshot (last step)
python -m F_render.src.render --step 0 --tag baseline # baseline of the longitudinal pair
python -m F_render.src.render --export                # + final 2-D PNG slices in figures/
python -m F_render.src.export_slices <hybrid_volume.json> --tag NAME

# real LIDC host (F-local masks + one free site, plan Q8; patient voxels stay in runs/)
python -m F_render.src.lidc download --n 20           # once; ~4.3 GB to ~/data/LIDC-IDRI
python -m F_render.src.host_masks --lidc LIDC-IDRI-0001
python -m F_render.src.fingerprint --masks F_render/runs/<ts>-host-LIDC-IDRI-0001/anatomy_masks.json --slice-thickness 2.5
python -m F_render.src.render --masks <…/anatomy_masks.json> --sites <…/sites.json> \
       --fingerprint <…-fingerprint/scanner_fingerprint.json> --tag lidc0001 --export

# #14 library (parameters only) → F_render/library/lesion_model_library.json
python -m F_render.src.lesion_fit --lidc 20           # ~1 h CPU

# reproductions (each updates status.json and writes its figure)
python -m F_render.repro.r13_synthetic_tumors
python -m F_render.repro.r14_lesion_fit
python -m F_render.repro.r15_fingerprint [--selfcheck]
python -m F_render.repro.r16_projection_vs_image      # ~45 min, XCIST
python -m F_render.repro.r17_naeotom_spectrum         # ~25 min, XCIST

Seeds.

  • Appearance (HU, texture, residual noise) comes from rng(certificate.extracted_seed_hex, "F.<label>").
  • Geometry (edge σ, lobulation, deformation, spicules) comes from rng(tumor_draw.shape_seed_hex, "F.<label>").
  • A fail certificate rejects the draw: exit code 2, nothing written.
  • The same inputs give a byte-identical hybrid_ct.nii.gz.

Claim level and honesty notes

Classical stage (claim level n/a).

  • Privacy-by-construction.
    • Only fitted parameters leave LIDC: library/lesion_model_library.json, about 4 KB of scalars.
    • LIDC pixel data live outside the repo (~/data/LIDC-IDRI). Hybrids of LIDC hosts stay in gitignored runs/.
    • The committed figures/render-lidc0001-*.png show a cropped slice of the public LIDC-IDRI scan 0001 (CC BY 3.0). That is a display export, not generator input.
    • Learned refiners (DiffTumor, MAISI) are ablation only and are not built.
  • F-local substitutes, replaced in INT.
    • Masks and the single site on LIDC hosts come from src/host_masks.py: thresholds + connected components, lobes not derivable (all 0), lobe label by z-half.
    • These are not A's lungmask/TotalSegmentator masks.
  • Image domain is the main path.
    • The projection-domain arm (#16) runs on a synthetic XCIST phantom with a Definition-like configuration from published parameters.
    • Real Mayo Siemens raw-data insertion is future work: it needs the TCIA agreement and the vendor geometry, and only Siemens cases may be used for Siemens work.
  • NAEOTOM Alpha (#17) is an XCIST approximation, not DukeSim. CdTe crosstalk and covariance are not modelled, and f50 does not match Br40 under the pre-registered kernel.
  • Missing sources. Solomon–Samei 2014, Sanders 2016 and Divel–Pelc 2019 are paywalled and not in papers/, so no number is claimed from them. F02, F03 and F04 were read as PMC full text.
  • Library HU. The solid HU mean (−22 HU) sits below soft tissue because of partial volume in small nodules on 2.5 mm slices. Ground-glass nodules fit the shape-only check poorly (corr 0.42); their realism comes from texture.

Pipeline readiness

Usable with caveats

Draft rating, not yet confirmed by the chain (the chain has not reached F). The image-domain insert reproduces the volume headline (+0.25 ± 1.02 %), and every chain flag exists (render --masks already accepts A's manifest). The runner asserts that the hybrid lies on A's host geometry (spacing, origin, direction, size). Two integration hazards showed up in the probe: --export writes host-derived PNGs into the git-tracked figures/, and the lesion library JSON is outside the commit's code hash.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [H01] Hu (label-free liver tumours): synthetic tumours good enough that segmentation AI trains without manual labels.
  • [F01] Ambrosini: fit nodule shape and HU models to real annotations.
  • [F05] Peng: generate realistic, position-dependent CT noise from the scan itself.
  • [F02] Robins, [F03] Mayo: insert nodules in the image domain vs the projection (raw-data) domain, and show both agree on volume.
  • [F04] McCabe (DukeSim): simulate the Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha photon-counting CT. [A06] Mayo low-dose CT images + raw projections.

Why it matters: a synthetic nodule is only useful if it looks like it was scanned by that scanner: the same blur, noise and partial-volume edges.

2. Contribution

  • Image-domain insertion reproduces the volume headline: +0.25 ± 1.02 % (projection arm +1.97 ± 1.32 %, synthetic XCIST phantom). evidence-based
  • Lesion shape model: 3-D correlation 0.8699 ± 0.0664 against the paper's 0.8897 ± 0.0609. evidence-based
  • Noise generator: σ and kurtosis within 2 %. NAEOTOM resolution is approximated but off (f50 +47 %). evidence-based
  • A privacy-by-construction library: about 4 KB of fitted scalars leave LIDC, and no patient voxels. evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: synthetic nodules that detectors and readers cannot tell from real ones, matched to each scanner's resolution, noise and dose, so sensitivity can be measured per scanner model and protocol, with exact masks. The upgrade path runs through photon-counting CT [F04]. extrapolation

4. Beyond lungs

  • Any CT organ. The insertion and fingerprint code is organ-agnostic. extrapolation
  • Other modalities. MR needs its own physics (signal model, coil noise), which is not built here; the same "fit parameters, never copy voxels" rule carries over. speculative
  • Dose and protocol studies. Re-render the same lesion at lower dose to find where detection breaks. extrapolation
  • Treatment planning QA. Lesions with known extent test auto-contouring for radiotherapy. extrapolation

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative F is the twin's imaging layer: predict what this patient's lesion would look like on another scanner, dose or reconstruction. Path: (1) image-domain insertion with a fitted fingerprint (now) → (2) raw-data insertion on vendor geometry [F03, A06] → (3) full scanner simulation [F04] → (4) virtual imaging trials on twin cohorts [H04, G02].

6. Predictions

5 years Assumptions: public LIDC/Mayo data; the XCIST simulator; no proprietary vendor geometry.

  • Image-domain volume agreement < 3 % holds (+0.25 %). evidence-based
  • Rendering with A's lungmask lobes replaces F-local threshold masks. extrapolation
  • Solid-nodule HU fitted on thinner slices fixes the −22 HU partial-volume bias. extrapolation

10 years Assumptions: access to vendor raw data and geometry (the Mayo Siemens path).

  • Projection-domain insertion becomes the default for scanner-specific studies. extrapolation
  • Photon-counting rendering matches the measured MTF. extrapolation

15 years Assumptions: fault-tolerant hardware.

  • speculative F stays classical: image physics gains nothing from quantum hardware in any scenario this project can argue for. The 15-year change is regulatory: rendered lesions accepted as evidence in virtual imaging trials [G02, H03].
